options.name: University degree
options.why: Your Bachelor pass lets you apply for degree programmes at public universities.
need: Bachelor pass with the subjects and points the course asks for
Certified ID and results
Application fee, where the university charges one
steps: Pick two or three courses and check their entry points
Check each university’s closing date
Apply online and track your application

options.name: University of technology: diploma or higher certificate
options.why: Shorter, career-focused programmes that need a lower pass level and lead to work or further study.
need: Diploma or Higher Certificate pass, or higher
Required subjects for the course
Certified ID and results
steps: List diploma courses in your field
Check minimum points and subjects
Apply before the closing date

options.name: TVET college
options.why: TVET colleges teach practical skills and trades, and many accept learners who did not get into university.
need: Matric results, or Grade 9 or 10 for some programmes
Certified ID
Proof of residence
steps: Find TVET colleges in your province
Choose a programme and check its entry rules
Apply at the college or online

link.label: Department of Higher Education and Training

options.name: Funding: NSFAS and bursaries
options.why: If paying is a problem, funding can cover fees at public universities and TVET colleges.
need: Household income within the funding limit
South African ID
A place or application at a public institution
steps: Check NSFAS rules and dates
Apply for NSFAS online
Search bursaries in your field and apply to several

options.name: Rewrite or improve your results
options.why: A fail, or a pass one level too low for your course, is not the end. You can rewrite subjects or improve your marks.
need: Your matric results
Registration for a rewrite or upgrade programme
Registration and exam fees, where they apply
steps: Find out which subjects to rewrite
Find the registration dates for the next sitting
Register and start studying

options.name: Learnership, internship or apprenticeship
options.why: You work and study at the same time, and you may earn a stipend while you learn.
need: Matric, usually with no specific pass level
Certified ID and CV
Often unemployed and aged 18 to 35
steps: Search learnership listings in your field
Check each one’s requirements
Send your CV and documents before the deadline

options.name: Private college or institute
options.why: Private institutions often have later or rolling intakes and offer many career-focused programmes. Fees are usually higher, and NSFAS does not pay for private colleges.
need: Matric results that meet the programme’s entry requirements
Certified ID
A way to pay fees, such as savings, a payment plan or a bursary
steps: Compare programmes and total fees
Check the intake and closing dates
Apply online and ask about payment plans and bursaries
